This project aims to develop a machine learning-based fake news detector that can accurately classify news articles.
The justification for this project lies in the increasing need to combat fake news and its societal implications.

This project is motivated by the challenge of detecting and classifying news articles as true or false, which is essential to maintain the integrity of news sources and prevent the damage caused by false information.
This project contributes to the field of natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning applications in real-world problems.
The objective of this project is to develop a machine learning-based fake news detector that can accurately classify news articles as true or false.
The problem addressed by this project is the need for an accurate, automated, and efficient method to identify fake news articles using machine learning techniques.

Future scope for this project includes exploring more advanced natural language processing techniques such as deep learning models (e.g., Recurrent Neural Networks, Transformers) for potentially higher accuracy, incorporating additional features like metadata or source reputation, evaluating the system on larger and more diverse datasets, developing methods for explaining the model's predictions, and potentially implementing the system in a real-world application accessible to users.
